sections.content: How many people stayed in Ledbury after gaining qualifications?

Ledbury is a small town in the West Midlands. Ledbury does not have its own university.

Ledbury has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Ledbury ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 335 state-school pupils from Ledbury who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 90 (27%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 110 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Ledbury to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Ledbury's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Ledbury in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Ledbury's GCSE cohort:

  • 40 graduates left the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 46% of graduates living in Ledbury had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 65 graduates from our cohort living in Ledbury, compared with the 90 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 54% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Ledbury, while 46% had moved there from elsewhere.
